playbook.title: How winners think
tips: Avoid round numbers — 5.00 and 10.00 get crowded fast.
A mid-low odd amount (like 7.37) often beats the pile-up at 1.00.
You can lock multiple sealed bids in one arena before the timer ends.

items.q: What does lowest unique bid mean?
items.a: When the arena closes we scan every sealed bid. The lowest amount that only one person chose wins — not the highest bid, and not a number two people tied on.
No. Bids stay sealed until reveal. You only ever see your own history inside an arena.
Activate once for {registrationFee} ETB. After that each sealed bid is {bidFee} ETB. Bid as many times as you want before the timer ends.
Any amount from 0.00 to {maxBid}.00 ETB. Unusual numbers beat crowded round ones.
After {days} days — the countdown is the only closer. Winner = lowest unique bid when the clock hits zero.

HowItWorks.title: How it works
HowItWorks.intro: BidClub is a lowest-unique-bid platform. Pick a sealed number that nobody can see, pay a small participation fee per bid, and if your number is the lowest one that nobody else picked, you win — then pay your winning bid amount to claim the prize.

items.title: Choose your bid amount
items.body: Pick any amount from 0.00 up to {maxBid}.00 ETB. Nobody else can see what you choose; it stays private until the arena closes.

items.title: Pay the bid fee
items.body: Each sealed bid costs a small participation fee (often around {bidFee} ETB, set per product). You can place as many sealed bids as you like before the timer ends.

items.title: Lowest unique bid wins
items.body: When the {days}-day timer hits zero, BidClub reveals every sealed bid. The lowest amount that only one person chose wins the prize.

example.title: See it in action
example.explanation: 2 was picked by two different bidders, so both 2s are eliminated. 5 was also picked twice, so it's out too. 4 and 7 were each picked by only one bidder, which makes them unique — and since 4 is lower than 7, 4 wins the prize.
